problem: "M̄_i has the same units as M per mole" reads as "(M per mole)", i.e. units per mole again (for example cm³/mol²), which is wrong. M is already a per-mole quantity, and M̄_i carries exactly the same units as M.
fix: "M̄_i carries the same units as M itself, because it is a property per mole of component i: if M is in cm³/mol then M̄_i is also in cm³/mol."

problem: The answer writes the tangent as y = M + (M̄₁ − M̄₂)(X − x₁) but never says what X is; a student can confuse X with the mixture property M or with x₁.
fix: Add: "Here X is a running value of the mole fraction along the tangent line, while M and dM/dx₁ are evaluated at the fixed composition x₁." Then substituting X = 1 gives M̄₁ and X = 0 gives M̄₂.
